prose_updates.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so a queried causal transfer is governed by the compatible fiber rather than by a selected numerical root. For odd \(m\), seed the queried edge and close only under graph-supported monomial variables that occur in its finite \(m\)-step remainders: noncollision and root-derivative separation on this exact terminating dependency set identify the transfer and yield simultaneous Wald disks. The directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path corridor is a readable sufficient superset and its earlier identification and Wald results remain corollaries. For even \(m\), the same-law sign obstruction continues to hold on the larger unrestricted stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovations. Exact transfer-aware certification and branch-free confidence-region inversion cover singular and nonregular cases.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either use non-Gaussian shocks for positive recovery, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Gong et al.'s positive theorem assumes non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, so neither it nor the present Gaussian supplied-order result contains the other. Prior root recursions also do not isolate, for one causal transfer, the exact finite set of graph-supported monomial dependencies induced by the known sampling factor.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular divided-difference recursion available. For the direct transfer, the sharp recursive locality is obtained by seeding \(u\to v\) and repeatedly adding only allowed off-diagonal variables that actually occur in retained \(m\)-step remainder monomials, together with their incident diagonals. This exact closure terminates, is contained in the directed path corridor, and can be strictly smaller; the path corridor remains an interpretable sufficient graphical screen.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit exact-dependency identifying map and simultaneous Wald disks on a nonempty compact class separated only on that finite set, while retaining the path-corridor and globally separated theorems as successive corollaries. It also gives an unrestricted stable-Gaussian even-sign obstruction with arbitrary positive-definite innovations, plus a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with attained witnesses and finite-sample branch-free inversion. The covariance-envelope fallback remains a validity device equal pathwise to the deterministic box, not a claimed adaptive improvement.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(M_0,M_1\) by overlapping empirical lag moments and form \(\widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1}\). On the odd regular class, compute the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\), recover only its incident diagonals and retained edges, propagate the Isserlis long-run covariance through that Jacobian, and report simultaneous Wald disks. The directed-path corridor and global derivative-separated estimators agree on the target and give simpler sufficient corollaries. Outside the exact-local regular class, invert the rationally outward-rounded moment box through all compatible fine-grid branches without selecting one.

prose_updates.related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate temporal causal recovery from subsampled data. Their positive recovery theorem uses non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions; the present positive result instead uses Gaussian innovations, a supplied order, and process-DAG restrictions, so the two positive classes are incomparable rather than related by inclusion. Their Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion motivates the obstruction, while the present proof isolates an even-factor sign pair on the strictly larger stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance and no order or triangularity requirement. Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) likewise use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods. Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints, whereas the present target is a numerical rational transfer. Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply triangular-root algorithms and branch theory; the new step derives the exact finite \(m\)-step graph-supported monomial dependency closure for one queried transfer, proves its terminating recursion, and retains the larger directed-path corridor as a readable corollary before combining graph zeros, innovation covariance, transfer equality, and complete-fiber certification. Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from an unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable. Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide concentration context for finite-sample moment regions. Mixed-frequency VARMA and unit-root results of Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) concern different model classes.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-dependency result still assumes a supplied scientifically defensible order and a known odd sampling factor for positive identification; it does not infer the order. The closure is exact for formal graph-supported monomial dependence in the stated triangular recursion, not a claim that every retained coefficient is numerically influential at every parameter value. Genericity is in fine-parameter space, not observed-law image space. Exact CAD certifies termination but not polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input. Gong et al.'s Temperature--Ozone example is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if external science supplies the one-way order; their fit does not establish that order, and their positive non-Gaussian theorem is not imported into this Gaussian class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Positive identification and Wald inference concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) process-DAG models with known odd subsampling factor and diagonal fine innovation covariance. Point identification and smooth recovery of \(h_{uv}\) require noncollision and derivative separation only on the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\). This closure is contained in, and can be strictly smaller than, the directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path corridor; the corridor and global separation results remain nonempty sufficient corollaries. Coefficients and innovation variances outside the relevant set may remain ambiguous, and no full-matrix uniqueness is claimed. In contrast, the even-factor sign obstruction holds for every stable Gaussian VAR(1) with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance, even without a supplied order, triangularity, or graph zeros, whenever the queried coordinate is nonzero. Outside the exact-local regular class, inference is branch-free. No claim is made about unknown sampling factors, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.
